title: OWASP Top 10 Kubernetes Security Risks Explained: Why Credentials Deserve a Closer Look
content_md: TL;DR K03 turns one leak into a chain : Secrets Management Failures let a single exposed token unlock more credentials. GitGuardian found 44 active clusters reachable through leaked secrets, and 30% had been exposed for over two years. Pipelines and repositories feed the cluster : GhostAction targeted 2,577 secret values across 772 repositories, and a public CISA-related repo exposed active credentials, showing how continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) and source control become paths into Kubernetes. Shrink the blast radius across the credential layer : Strict RBAC, short-lived workload identity, and credential detection across repos, images, and pipelines limit what any exposed token can reach, with ggshield, AI hooks, and Developer Endpoint Protection preventing new leaks. Recent attacks make the OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 essential reading Kubernetes powers modern infrastructure. 82% of container users now run it in production environments, according to the most recent Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Annual Cloud Native Survey . For the majority of DevOps teams who want to run their applications in containers, Kubernetes is the first thing they turn to. Kubernetes (K8s) offers many advantages, but it also has potential pitfalls if you don't set everything up correctly. This is why Kubernetes has its own OWASP Top 10.
